Projected sea level change under climate scenarios from IPCC Assessment Report 6

Source: R/data.R
ar6_us_compiled_scenarios.Rd

Probabilistic and localized relative sea-level rise scenarios produced for NOAA tide gauges for the 6th IPCC Assesment Report by Kopp and Garner (2023). Scenarios were reprocessed by James Holmquist into long-form tables that could be more readily queried.

Usage

ar6_us_compiled_scenarios

Format

A data frame with 2,278,458 rows and 10 columns:

psmsl_id

Unique permanant service for mean sea level identifier

latitude

Gauge latitude in decimal degrees WGS84.

longitude

Gauge longitude in decimal degrees WGS84.

year

Calendar year (YYYY)

quantile

Value between 0 and 1 indicating position of the sea-level rise magnitude within the probability space of the scnenario.

sea_level_change_mm

Sea level change relative to the baseline period (1986–2005)

noaa_id

Unique NOOA numeric station identifier

noaa_name

Unique NOAA station name

scenario_name

Unique scenario name indicating a Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (ssp) or temperature limitation window (tlim). See source data for additional detail.

confidence

Indicates whether forecats are made propegating uncertainty at 'medium' or 'low' confidence

Source

Kopp, R. E., Garner, G. G., Hermans, T. H., Jha, S., Kumar, P., Reedy, A., ... & Smith, C. (2023). The Framework for Assessing Changes To Sea-level (FACTS) v1. 0: a platform for characterizing parametric and structural uncertainty in future global, relative, and extreme sea-level change. Geoscientific Model Development, 16(24), 7461-7489.

Reformatted in https://github.com/Smithsonian/Tidal_Scenarios, by James Holmquist
